verses.53:1: Who has believed what we have heard? And the arm of the LORD, to whom has it been revealed?
verses.53:2: He grew up before Him like a young shoot, and like a root out of parched ground. He had no form and no splendor; and when we looked at him, there was no appearance that we should find him desirable.
verses.53:3: He was despised and abandoned by people, a man of pains and familiar with sickness; and like one from whom faces are hidden, he was despised, and we did not value him.
verses.53:4: Yet surely it was our sicknesses that he bore, and our pains that he carried; but we ourselves regarded him as stricken, struck down by God, and afflicted.
verses.53:5: But he was pierced because of our transgressions, crushed because of our iniquities; the discipline for our peace was on him, and by his welts healing has come to us.
verses.53:6: All of us have strayed like sheep; we have turned, each one, to his own way; and the LORD has made the iniquity of us all land on him.
verses.53:7: He was oppressed, and he was afflicted, yet he would not open his mouth; like a lamb that is led to the slaughter, and like a ewe that is silent before her shearers, he would not open his mouth.
verses.53:8: By restraint and judgment he was taken away; and as for his generation, who considered it? For he was cut off from the land of the living; because of the transgression of my people the blow fell on him.
verses.53:9: And they assigned his grave with the wicked, and with a rich man in his deaths, although he had done no violence, and there was no deceit in his mouth.
verses.53:10: Yet the LORD was pleased to crush him; He made him sick. If his soul makes a guilt offering, he will see offspring, he will lengthen his days, and the pleasure of the LORD will succeed in his hand.
verses.53:11: Because of the anguish of his soul he will see, he will be satisfied; by his knowledge the righteous one, My servant, will make the many righteous, and he himself will carry their iniquities.
verses.53:12: Therefore I will give him a portion among the many, and with the mighty he will divide the spoil, because he laid bare his soul to death and was counted with the transgressors; yet he himself bore the sin of many, and for the transgressors he will intercede.

notes.53:1: Shemu'athenu can mean "our report" or "what was heard by us." The Hebrew puts "the arm of the LORD" first in its clause, and that order is kept.
notes.53:2: Lowercase pronouns are used for the servant and capitals for the LORD ("before Him"). The Hebrew does not mark the servant as divine, and the case keeps the two referents apart in verses such as 53:10. The clause break after "splendor" follows the Masoretic athnach accent under hadar.
notes.53:3: Makh'oboth and choli mean "pains" and "sickness"; they are rendered the same way in 53:4. Chadal ishim is literally "ceasing from / lacking men," that is, abandoned by people. Master panim mimmennu is literally "a hiding of faces from him."
notes.53:5: Mecholal means "pierced" or "wounded"; the preposition min here means "because of." Musar is discipline or chastening. Nirpa-lanu is an impersonal passive: "it is healed for us," so "healing has come to us." Chavurah is a welt or bruise from blows.
notes.53:6: Hifgia bo means "made to meet / strike against him"; "made ... land on him" keeps the image of a burden falling on him. The same verb appears in 53:12, where it means "intercede."
notes.53:7: Niggas means "oppressed" or "hard pressed"; na'aneh is passive ("afflicted") but may be reflexive ("he let himself be afflicted"). The repeated imperfect lo yiftach is rendered "would not open" to bring out that he chose silence.
notes.53:8: This verse is difficult. Me'otser umimmishpat may mean "by oppression and judgment" or "without restraint and without justice." Doro ("his generation") may mean his contemporaries or his descendants, and yesocheach means "consider" or "complain." Lamo is literally "to them" (or a poetic "to him"); "on him" follows the sense required by the context. The Hebrew has "my people," spoken by the prophet or the LORD.
notes.53:9: Wayyitten is impersonal, "one gave," rendered "they assigned." Bemothaw is a plural, "in his deaths," which may be intensive (a violent death) or may mean "his tomb"; the Hebrew plural is kept.
notes.53:10: Hecheli is "He made (him) sick," from the same root as choli in 53:3–4. Tasim is either third person feminine with nafsho ("his soul") as subject ("if his soul makes a guilt offering," followed here) or second person addressed to the LORD ("if You make his soul a guilt offering"). Asham is the guilt (reparation) offering of Lev 5.
notes.53:11: The Masoretic Text has "he will see" with no object; the Qumran scroll 1QIsa-a and the Septuagint add "light." Since this column translates only the Hebrew, "light" is not supplied. Yatsdiq tsaddiq is a wordplay: "the righteous one will make righteous." Beda'to can mean "by his knowledge" or "by knowing him."
notes.53:12: He'erah means "laid bare" or "poured out" (Gen 24:20). Yafgia is the verb of 53:6, here meaning to intercede or intervene.
